tasks.short: Evaluate student work and provide checked grades and feedback

steps.what: Evaluate students' class work, laboratory work, assignments and papers against explicit criteria
outputs: lecturer grading decisions and evidence notes

steps.what: Draft criterion-linked feedback from the lecturer's evaluated work and evidence notes
inputs: lecturer grading decisions and evidence notes

loop.input: Criterion decisions and evidence notes linked to the exact submission
loop.output: Draft feedback without new grade decisions
loop.check: Lecturer checks every observation and recommendation against the student's work and intended grading rationale
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported feedback returns to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed comments cannot express all submission-specific explanations

steps.what: Check feedback and grade records before releasing results to students
inputs: lecturer grading decisions and evidence notes

tasks.design: Use native comment banks in {LMS} first, with bounded drafting only for explanations based on the lecturer's decisions in {DOCS}. Keep all evaluation and grade decisions human, and release only the checked submission-specific version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing individual explanations follows substantive evaluation and can be repetitive.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning platforms can draft feedback from instructor notes.
tasks.still_hard: Judge scientific reasoning and distinguish weak evidence from a different valid approach.
tasks.human_edge: Own fair assessment and useful feedback.
tasks.altitude: Protect grading judgement while reducing limited feedback phrasing work.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this supports phrasing assistance, not autonomous grade decisions.
The modest time effect is unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the lecturer produces submission ID and version, criterion decisions, proposed grade, evidence locations and intended improvement points; its 65 hours includes capture and assessment.
The 14 remaining hours in s2 include checking and repairing draft phrasing; s3 retains release checks separately.
Missing evidence or doubtful feedback returns to manual comments; no automatic student performance or misconduct flag is used.
Use native comment banks before adding a model; four added focal hours cover calibration, source-access checks and drafting upkeep.
Any dual-system grade entry remains in s3 and receives no assumed integration saving.
research_questions: Does note-based feedback drafting save time after assessment, repairs and release checks?

approvals.approved_version: Exact student submission ID and version, grade, criterion rationale, feedback text and recipient; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=94; gross 6 minus 4 focal upkeep gives central net 2. E1 range 0-1 allows minimal phrasing burden or extensive repairs; grading retains full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise and assist students during regular office hours

steps.what: Maintain regularly scheduled office hours to advise and assist students with individual questions

tasks.design: Retain individual advising and assistance using {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}. Regular availability and responsive conversation are the baseline; no large appointment-booking burden is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Students need individual clarification and contextual advice.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calendars and course records support regular access.
tasks.still_hard: Understand the student's difficulty and agree useful next steps.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, adapt explanations and recognise support needs.

evidence.claim: Individual advising retains full time; existing scheduling tools establish no new saving in the conversation.

assumptions: The baseline is office-hour availability and assistance rather than an invented scheduling process.
No new service or maintenance is added.
research_questions: Is repetitive scheduling measurable outside the advising conversation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Individual advising and assistance remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions while responding to students' reasoning

tasks.design: Keep live discussion facilitation with the lecturer using {DOCS} reference material. Prepared prompts support the activity without replacing responsiveness to students or claiming a new preparation baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful discussion depends on participation, misconceptions and evolving arguments.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing course materials provide discussion context.
tasks.still_hard: Balance participation and challenge reasoning constructively.
tasks.human_edge: Respond to the class and create space for productive disagreement.

evidence.claim: Live discussion facilitation retains full time in this design.

assumptions: Student contributions arise in the discussion; no preclassified argument or comprehension score is assumed.
Course-material preparation is outside this live facilitation baseline.
No new automation service or upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: What support improves discussion quality without replacing live facilitation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Live facilitation remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and revise agricultural sciences curricula and instruction

steps.what: Evaluate curricula, course content and instructional methods and define evidence-based revision goals
Draft revised course content, materials and instructional options from the lecturer's brief

loop.purpose: Develop candidate course revisions from selected goals and sources
loop.input: Checked brief, existing materials and permitted source excerpts
loop.output: Draft revisions with source links and explicit gaps
loop.check: Lecturer verifies scientific accuracy, learning alignment, workload and accessibility
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported content or poor learning alignment returns to manual design
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise a course but cannot express varied examples and instructional options

steps.what: Plan and select curriculum revisions after checking materials and instructional feasibility
outputs: selected materials and methods for further approval

tasks.design: Use native course structures in {LMS} and templates in {DOCS}, adding bounded drafting for varied examples and revision options. The lecturer evaluates evidence and chooses revisions; formal curriculum adoption and publication remain outside the draft workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning selected educational goals into alternative materials takes drafting effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can propose examples and wording from a checked source brief.
tasks.still_hard: Determine whether changes improve learning and remain scientifically sound.
tasks.human_edge: Choose educational priorities and evaluate classroom feasibility.
tasks.altitude: Spend less initial drafting time while retaining curriculum evaluation.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting can produce candidate course revisions; the task-specific design and savings are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the lecturer captures course version, learning outcomes, observed problems, permitted sources, required changes, constraints and success criteria; its 35 hours includes evidence evaluation and brief preparation.
No student learning-gap flag or evaluated curriculum brief is assumed to appear without the lecturer's work.
The 21 remaining hours in s2 include scientific and pedagogical draft repair; s3 retains final selection and feasibility checks.
Use native course templates and existing materials before model drafting; six extra focal hours cover source, prompt and example upkeep.
Missing evidence returns to manual design; no autonomous grading, curriculum adoption or publication is proposed.
research_questions: Does bounded revision drafting save time after source preparation and pedagogical checks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=86; gross 14 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 8. E1 range 0-4 allows one-off materials and extensive pedagogical repair; evaluation and selection remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Assist feedback phrasing and course drafting while retaining assessment, curriculum judgement and student interaction.
role.ambitious_version: An agricultural sciences lecturer who uses checked drafts to reduce limited writing effort and retains responsibility for learning, grades and student support.
